extracted.intended_audience: judge advocates, convening authorities, and military officers responsible for drafting charges and conducting courts-martial
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal standards for preparing, amending, serving, and trying military charges and specifications, and for constituting courts-martial (composition, judge advocate selection, timing, pleadings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification must identify preferring officer when using 'me'
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a specification preferred by a superior against an inferior refers to the former as 'me' and alleges the accused addressed abusive language to 'me' or assaulted 'me' without naming or otherwise indicating the subject, such a form is not sanctioned and, on objection, the court should require amendment or add the name of the preferring officer when incorporating the charge in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by some English precedents but not our practice; cure by amendment or addition of name. (R. 3, 429, Aug., 1863.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Accused's name need only identify unambiguously
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not essential to state the full Christian name of the accused; only such name or initial need be given as will be sufficient unmistakably to identify the party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial names/initials acceptable if they identify the individual. (R. 24, 299, Feb., 1867; C. 16974, Oct. 5, 1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification should aver time and place of offense
rubrics_metrics.description: The time and place of the commission of the offense charged should properly be averred so it appears the offense was committed within the period of limitation and to enable the accused to understand what particular act or omission he is called upon to defend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for statute of limitations and for ability to plead former acquittal/conviction. (R. 1, 463, Dec. 1862; 5, 613, Jan., 1864.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'on or about' / 'at or near' when exact time/place unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the exact time or place is not known, it is frequently preferable to allege it as having occurred 'on or about' a certain date or 'at or near' a certain locality rather than naming a specific day or place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These phrases indicate a period as nearly as can be ascertained; avoid unnecessary use when exact time/place is known. (R. 26, 437, Feb., 1868.)

rubrics_metrics.name: No precise legal construction for 'on or about'
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no defined construction to be placed upon the words 'on or about'; the phrase cannot be said to cover any precise number of days or latitude in time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to indicate a period when exact day cannot be named; same applies to 'at or near' for place. (R. 26, 437, Feb., 1868.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Allege continuous offenses over a period when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: When the offense charged consists of acts committed over time (e.g., improper disposition of public property while en route), allegations that the offense occurred between dates or over a route are sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate where commission was not on any particular day but over a span. (R. 25, 100, Sept., 1867.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of time important for desertion/absence cases
rubrics_metrics.description: A reasonably exact allegation of the time is important in cases such as desertion and absence without leave to enable the accused later to plead former acquittal or conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise dating helps protect against double prosecution and supports later defenses. (R. 7, 348 and 513, Apr., 1864.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegation of time should be as definite as facts permit
rubrics_metrics.description: The allegation of time in a specification should be as nearly defined as the facts will permit; where acts extended over a considerable time, it may be necessary to cover the whole period in the allegation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of 'from March to September' countenanced for continuous neglect of duty. (P. 31, 357, Apr., 1889.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Less exactness required for offenses of omission
rubrics_metrics.description: When the offense charged is one of omission rather than a single specific act, it is generally sufficient to allege that the offense occurred between certain named dates not unreasonably separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Omissions can be pleaded by covering a reasonable interval. (R. 30, 488, July, 1870.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overly vague multi-day allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Alleging that the accused was drunk on duty 'at some time or times during a period of 70 days' is insufficient notice and renders the specification uncertain and insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific instances or narrower periods are required for adequate notice. (R. 1, 463, Dec., 1862.)

rubrics_metrics.name: May note immediate result/effect as descriptive circumstance
rubrics_metrics.description: While pleading matter of evidence is generally irregular, there is no objection to noting in brief in the specification the immediate result or effect of the act charged as a circumstance of description illustrating character and extent of the offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., a capital homicide connected with a military offense may be stated in conclusion as aggravation and indicating animus or force used. (R. 34, 478, Sept., 1873.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not charge a secondary offense in lieu of the principal offense
rubrics_metrics.description: It is illogical and faulty pleading to charge a secondary offense in lieu of the actual or principal offense when the charged offense is merely a consequence or incident of the principal offense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such charging is defective; principal offense should be charged. (R. 27, 446, Jan., 1869.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid undue multiplication of charges
rubrics_metrics.description: Undue multiplication of charges or forms of charge is to be avoided; charges should not generally be added for minor offenses that are simply acts included in and going to make up graver offenses duly charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not add separate minor charges when they are part of a graver charged offense. (R. 15, 441, July, 1865.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not phrase charges in the alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: A charge or specification should not be expressed in the alternative (e.g., 'did sell or through neglect lose'); selling, losing through neglect, and spoiling through neglect are distinct offenses and should be separately charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative phrasing is irregular and defective and may be struck out or required to be amended. (P. 28, 35, 110, Nov., 1888; multiple later citations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid signing charges 'by order of' another officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing charges with the name of an officer adding 'by the order of' his commander is unusual and not recommended; charges not signed voluntarily by the preferring officer are usually subscribed by the judge advocate of the court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge Advocate General's Office prepares charges but does not sign them; authentication usually by acting judge advocate or judge advocate of the court. (R. 34, 598, Nov., 1873; R. 47, 521, Sept., 1884.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Disrespect under article 20 must be particularized
rubrics_metrics.description: Disrespect under the twentieth article may consist of acts or words; the particular acts or words relied on as constituting the offense should properly be set forth in substance in the specification, and evidence must show the officer offended against was the 'commanding officer' of the accused.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition of 'commanding officer' clarified by context (temporary detachments, etc.). (Multiple citations.)

rubrics_metrics.name: In assault causing death include 'thereby causing his death' as aggravation
rubrics_metrics.description: When charging striking or doing violence to a superior officer under article 21, where the assault was fatal, it is allowable to add 'thereby causing his death' to indicate the measure of violence employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show extent of force; appropriate as part of specification. (R. 29, 485, Dec., 1869.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Courts will judicially notice state of war in some charges
rubrics_metrics.description: In framing a charge under certain articles, it is generally not essential to allege that the act was committed in time of war, etc.; this is a fact of which a court will ordinarily take judicial notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in several articles; not necessary to plead state of war if clearly a judicially noticeable fact. (R. 17, 396, Oct., 1865; C. 13309, etc.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Misappropriation of public funds does not require intent to defraud
rubrics_metrics.description: In framing a charge under article 60 for knowingly and willfully misappropriating public funds, it is not necessary to allege an intent to defraud the United States; the act described constitutes the offense irrespective of motive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charge looks to the act of misappropriation itself. (R. 5, 498, Dec., 1863; C. 23277, Nov. 30, 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: No need to aver property was for military service if apparent
rubrics_metrics.description: In charging embezzlement under the sixtieth article, it is not necessary to aver in terms that the money or property was 'furnished or intended for the military service' if that fact sufficiently appears from other allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive facts elsewhere in specification can supply this element. (R. 47, 476, Sept. 1884.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Abusive language under article 61 must be particularized to show gravity
rubrics_metrics.description: Abusive language toward a commanding officer may constitute an offense under article 61, but the language should be so particularized as to show it constituted a graver offense than mere disrespect; otherwise the specification is subject to a motion to make definite or strike out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleadings must set forth and characterize the epithets or words employed. (R. 56, 562, Sept., 1888.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Drunkenness off-duty charged under article 62 unless circumstances elevate it
rubrics_metrics.description: Drunkenness not on duty, when off duty but amounting to a 'disorder,' should be charged under article 62 unless, in the case of an officer, committed under such circumstances as to constitute an offense under article 61.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context determines article selection. (R. 31, 52, Nov., 1870.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility in phrasing article 62 charges but must set forth facts
rubrics_metrics.description: A crime, disorder, or neglect cognizable under article 62 may be charged by name, by name with 'to the prejudice of good order and military discipline,' simply as 'conduct to the prejudice of good order and military discipline,' or as 'violation of the sixty-second article of war.' It is immaterial which form if the specification sets forth facts constituting an act prejudicial to good order and discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When charge and specification together make out such an act, pleading regarded as substantially sufficient. (R. 7, 485, Mar., 1864; others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot plead simply prior convictions/habits as specification under article 62
rubrics_metrics.description: A charge of 'conduct to the prejudice' with a specification setting forth merely trials and convictions for previous offenses (or 'habitual drunkenness' with instances of past sentences) is not a pleading of an offense under article 62; such aggregation or repetition contravenes double jeopardy principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifications alleging 'frequently' drunk or 'frequent' absences should be struck out; correct pleading is general charge with separate specifications of particular instances. (R. 27, 531, Nov., 1868; R. 36, 142, May, 1875; R. 38, 211, Aug., 1876.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Breach of Army regulation imposing a duty may be charged under article 62
rubrics_metrics.description: A breach of an Army regulation that imposes a duty upon an officer or soldier is in general chargeable as 'conduct to the prejudice of good order and military discipline' and punishable under article 62.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory breaches that prejudice discipline fall under article 62. (R. 39, 283, Nov., 1877; G. 19330, Mar. 10, 1906.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of article 61 prosecutions for officers
rubrics_metrics.description: In bringing an officer to trial under the sixty-first article the chief purpose is to obtain the court's judgment upon the character of his acts or conduct from the point of view of that article; if his conduct also constitutes a crime, that criminal offense should be charged under the proper article for additional punishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Article 61 focuses on character/unbecoming conduct; separate criminal charges may be added. (C. 17667, Mar. 18, 1905.)

rubrics_metrics.name: General prisoners are civilians for article 21 purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: General prisoners who have been dishonorably discharged and are held in execution of imprisonment at hard labor are citizens and cannot commit acts in violation of the twenty-first article of war; acts of disobedience by general prisoners should be charged under article 62.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different status changes applicable article. (C. 16220, Apr. 26, 1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: List of proposed witnesses not part of the charge but may be appended
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of proposed witnesses is no part of the military charge, though it may properly be appended; in serving a copy of the charges to the accused it is not essential, though better practice, to add a copy of the list of witnesses when appended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appending the list does not preclude calling witnesses not named. (R. 25, 350, Feb., 1868.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid long dormancy of charges; try promptly
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reprehensible to allow charges to lie long dormant before being preferred; charges should be brought to trial as soon as practicable and while evidence is fresh; a delay of five months was remarked upon as prejudicial and unfair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt preference and trial recommended; exceptions for slight offenses where showing a course of conduct may warrant delay but not unreasonably prolonged. (P. 24, 283, May, 1888; R. 12, 348, Feb., 1865.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'saving up' or accumulation of charges from hostile animus
rubrics_metrics.description: Waiting to prefer charges until a series of similar acts have been committed may be expedient for slight offenses, provided the period is not unreasonably prolonged; however, accumulation or saving up of charges through hostile animus is discouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecutorial fairness required; prefer and try charges immediately in general. (R. 12, 348, Feb., 1865; C. 17667, Mar. 18, 1905.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation-required statements to convening authority are not character declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: The statements as to enlistments, discharges, etc., required by Army Regulations to be furnished with the original charge to the convening authority are not intended to be accompanied by a declaration as to the officer's present character; the regulation does not call for the officer's opinion on the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character of the accused is not to be considered at this stage. (P. 39, 459, Mar., 1890; 43, 10, Sept., 1890.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Material amendment should be made before actual trial
rubrics_metrics.description: A material amendment of a charge should properly be made before the actual trial; amending a specification after trial and arraigning the accused nunc pro tunc is without law or precedent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments of form may be made after arraignment with assent; slight amendments of substance allowed; substantial amendments that materially modify the matter before the court usually not authorized and any amendment of substance should be allowed with caution and with accused's right to apply for continuance. (B. 48, 315, Feb., 1884.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Middle name/initial misnomer is generally immaterial
rubrics_metrics.description: A middle name or initial is no part of a person's name in law, and except where necessary to identify the individual may be omitted from the charge; an erroneous middle name or initial may be disregarded unless the accused moves to strike or objects, in which case he must state his true name and the charge may be amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Misnomers can be amended in court without delaying proceedings if objection is made. (P. 34, 440, Aug., 1889; B. 52, 675, Oct., 1887.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of charges does not legally bar re-preferment
rubrics_metrics.description: A withdrawal of charges constitutes no legal bar to their being subsequently revived and re-preferred; charges once formally withdrawn will not in general properly be revived except upon new material evidence; charges accepted as sufficient by a convening commander cannot be withdrawn except by his authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical restraints on revival; convening authority control. (B. 11, 202, Dec., 1864; B. 21, 56, Nov., 1865.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Original charges are public documents and deposited with judge advocate
rubrics_metrics.description: The original charges referred to a court-martial are a public document; after arraignment and copying into the record, the original charges have served their purpose and the place of deposit for this public record is the office of the judge advocate of the convening authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original serves as public record; deposit location specified. (C. 15833, Jan. 28, 1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations about court constitution are mandatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations which relate to the constitution of the court and not merely to the method of procedure are always mandatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constitutional/regulatory requirements for courts must be followed. (O. 5325, Nov. 15, 1898; others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: President's authority to convene general courts-martial
rubrics_metrics.description: The President is empowered to convene general courts-martial generally, by virtue of his authority as Commander in Chief; convening a court-martial is an executive act (order) to certain officers to assemble and exercise powers conferred by the Articles of War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This general power has been exercised repeatedly and is legal when made through head of executive department. (R. 33, 603, Dec., 1872; multiple orders cited.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications for trial under §1230 R.S. must be made within reasonable time
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1230 R.S. provides for trial by court-martial, upon application, of officers dismissed by order of the President but does not indicate the period after dismissal; only applications made within a reasonable time will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonableness determined by circumstances. (R. 16, 170, Mar., 1860; others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer officers' requests for trial may lapse after muster out
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for trial by court-martial under section 1280 R.S. by a volunteer officer who had been dismissed cannot be entertained after the Volunteer Army has been mustered out because the officers become civilians and Army laws no longer apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness linked to military status. (C. 4454, Jan. 20 and Feb. 4, 1899.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Officers of certain branches subject to detail only by War Department orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers of the branches of the service specified in regulations are subject to be detailed upon court-martial duty only by orders emanating from the War Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local orders that merely request report do not exempt or place such officers under a command for court-martial service. (P. 48, 255, July, 1891.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid detailing same officers to multiple courts without dissolving
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailing as a court-martial the same officers as those already constituting a court (without dissolving the first) should not be resorted to if avoidable; same applies to detailing a single officer upon two distinct courts at the same time unless unavoidable due to scarcity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice discouraged though precedents exist; avoid embarrassment to service. (R. 7, 134, Feb., 1864; 19, 495, Mar., 1866.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations may be tried by courts containing volunteer officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations may be tried by a court-martial upon which volunteer officers sit as members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases where volunteer officers sat on courts trying regulations. (C. 13649, Nov. 11, 1902; others.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Only officers can be detailed as court members; avoid biased members
rubrics_metrics.description: Only officers can be detailed as members of courts-martial; chaplains and certain acting assistant grades are not usually eligible; officers who are biased or interested in the case should not be detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility rules and conflict-of-interest considerations. (R. 36, 450, Mar. 8, 1875; R. 22, 542, Dec., 1866; R. 39, 240, Oct. 22, 1877.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Convening authority is sole judge on availability of superior members
rubrics_metrics.description: The convening authority is the sole judge of whether it is possible to constitute a court of members all superior in rank to the accused, and his decision as indicated by the convening order is conclusive upon the court on that matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court bound by convening order's determination. (R. 3, 82, June, 1863; C. 10910, Aug. 17, 1901; C. 21079, Oct. 12, 1908.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Medical/dental officers eligible but should be avoided if practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: A Medical Reserve Corps officer lawfully on active duty, or a dental surgeon commissioned as such, is legally eligible for detail as a member of a general court-martial or as a trial officer of a summary court; however, medical officers should not be detailed when it can be avoided because their duties to the sick may interfere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility recognized but prudence advised. (a 23135, Nov. 27, 1911; R. 22, 536, Dec., 1866.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Any commissioned officer may be judge advocate; avoid conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any commissioned officer may legally be appointed judge advocate of a court-martial (including surgeons or chaplains), but an officer should not act as judge advocate in a case in which he is personally interested as accuser or prosecutor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While civilians have been employed historically, such employment is now rare/limited; judge advocates who prepared charges and are personally prejudiced should not act. (R. 9, 377, July, 1864; P. 39, 35, Feb., 1890; R. 4, 413, Dec., 1885.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Select judge advocate without considerable prejudice or interest
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable to detail as judge advocate, if practicable, an officer who has no considerable prejudice against the party to be tried or any decided personal interest in his case; selection of a materially interested officer is unfortunate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid selecting officers who are material witnesses or would personally benefit by conviction. (R. 21, 177, Jan., 1866; R. 31, 361, May, 1871.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge advocate may be relieved pending trial but not changed after trial for record authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: While a judge advocate may be relieved pending a trial and a new one appointed, it would not be proper to make such a change after conclusion of the trial simply for the purpose of having the record authenticated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-trial substitution for authentication is improper. (C. 5230, Oct., 1898; C. 17038, Oct. 18, 1904.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of a court-martial cannot be routinely delegated to a staff officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of a court-martial cannot be legally delegated to a staff officer as a routine duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convening authority must perform appointment authority; delegation inappropriate. (C. 1499, July 17, 1895.)
